Commentary.Commentary: We are set to resume the game. England players have made their way out in the middle. Imam-ul-Haq and Abdullah Shafique start for Pakistan. James Anderson comes to bowl. Here we go.
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Right then, England have ensured that Pakistan will have a tough time if they want to win the game from here. Pakistan will need to come out with something special here. We'll be back soon for Pakistan's response.

Pakistan bowlers were good from the start and bagged some early wickets. Naseem Shah was the pick of the bowlers for Pakistan with figures of 3 for 140. Zahid Mahmood claimed four wickets but also became the bowler who conceded the post runs on his debut having given an excess of 200. Not good numbers from the Pakistan bowlers on a whole but they will be hoping on their batters can now put up a good opening stand for them. They surely bounced back from what happened on Day 1.

Finally, England's innings has come to an end. They have recorded their best score so far in Test Cricket against Pakistan. Some positives to take out from this outing for the hosts is that they were really good with the ball in this session. England have posted a mammoth total of 657 here and Pakistan certainly have a task to do. The vistors continued their 'Bazball' approach but lost Ben Stokes pretty early in the day. Liam Livingstone could not make much of an impact on his debut and followed his skipper back to the pavilion. Harry Brook was the man to watch for as he went absolutely berseck getting to his maided 150. There has to be a special mention of the over from Zahid Mahmood where Harry Brook scored 27 runs off it. He was finally dismissed on 153 off just 113 balls and a small cameo from Will Jacks and Ollie Robinson helped England grow in strength.

Multiple records tumbled along the way in this game and we shall dig into some of them to understand the magnitude of England's effort. First and foremost, we shall focus on the massive total that the team achieved, which is the highest that has been scored on Day 1 of the Test match as no team has been able to cross the 500-run mark. The fact that the visitors achieved it with 15 overs unused in the day, makes the achievement even more special. With Zak Crawley, Ben Duckett, Ollie Pope, and Harry Brook all reaching centuries, they created the record for the most batters to score a hundred runs on Day 1 of a Test match as four of them were able to do it. The 200-plus partnership between the openers was scored at a run rate of 6.53, which is the highest for any opening partnership which is 200 runs or more. We have another day of excitement close at hand and we are certain some more records will be collected on the way. Do stay with us as we return shortly for the morning session of Day 2.

On Day 1, the visitors won the toss and despite Ben Stokes’ preference to chase targets in the fourth innings, he made the right decision to bat first on what appeared to be a dead track. Right from the start, the England openers looked to be positive and go after the bowlers. The Zak Crawley-Ben Duckett partnership accumulated 233 at better than a run every ball with both of them reaching centuries and Pakistan were able to get the breakthrough only in the second session. The hosts dismissed the openers in quick succession and even claimed the priced wicket of Joe Root in the middle session but lost momentum once again as Ollie Pope and Harry Brook came on to score tons as well. Ollie Pope was dismissed after his hundred but that got the captain Ben Stokes at the crease and he began producing an exhibition of 'Bazball' cricket. The scoreboard reads 506/4 at the end of Day 1 and Pakistan never looked in control of the game. Their bowlers failed to find the right length to bowl on this wicket and will be hoping to bounce back with some quick wickets in the first session. Three debutants claimed wickets yesterday with Zahid Mahmood picking up two and the two pacers, Haris Rauf and Mohammad Ali chipping in with one each.

Hello and welcome back, ladies and gentlemen to our coverage of Day 2 of the first Test in this historic series between Pakistan and England. It will be the visitors who would have slept well after their performance on Day 1 and with the bout of illness they had experienced before the game started, it is a good thing they are rested. Pakistan were completely outplayed but they would have to look deep at the flatness of the pitch. With them needing to win 4 of the 5 remaining games to make it to the finals of the World Test Championship, a batting paradise does very little good for their chances. That said they will be looking to come out and take this new day as an opportunity to start over.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

That is all we have from this opening day of the first Test match which has been an absolute run-fest. Pakistan have loads to do on Day 2 if they are to claw themselves back into this game. Will we witness a fightback from the hosts? Or will England consolidate their position even further? We shall find out when the play resumes on Friday, 2nd of December at 10.30 am IST (5 am GMT). Do join us for the build-up which begins well in advance. Cheers!

Right then, the first session will be really crucial for Pakistan if they are to have a chance in this game as they need early wickets. The new ball will be available in 5 more overs and if they are unable to get any reverse swing early they may opt to take it. England have some dangerous batters in their ranks and if they are not contained they could reach a massive total in really quick time. Their newfound positive approach has put them in a strong position and things have to go really wrong if they are to lose from here.

The day has well and truly belonged to England and it was courtesy of an outstanding start from the openers who accumulated runs at will. The first session yielded over 170 runs and Pakistan looked like they were incapable of claiming a wicket. The second session was more or less the same for close to an hour but when the partnership was broken and both the openers were dismissed in quick succession, Pakistan may have felt that they had an opening. They got the big wicket of Joe Root as well but Ollie Pope and Harry Brook consolidated the inning going into the Tea break.

England came out for the last session with Harry Brook and Ollie Pope looking to build on their partnership and it looked like they were in no mood to take it slow as they put on a 176-run stand in just 149 balls. Ollie Pope reached his ton and was dismissed shortly afterward by Mohammad Ali who has had a debut to forget but will definitely remember his first wicket. Harry Brook continued the onslaught even smashing four boundaries in one over bowled by and unfortunate Saud Shakeel. He raced to his century and reached there in 80 balls with Ben Stokes coming in to add to Pakistan's woes. The play was stopped with 15 overs in the day still left due to bad light but it felt like the umpires were saving the Pakistan bowlers from further drubbing.

Session Summary - 21 overs, 174 runs, and 1 wicket. Another session which was dominated by the English batters and Pakistan do not seem to be getting a break. Two more centurions in their ranks which makes it the first time four batters have reached hundreds on Day 1 of a Test match and Joe Root will be feeling left out. England scored more than 8 runs per over in the final session and have crossed the 500-run mark, the first time this has been achieved on Day 1 of a Test match. A day full of records and we have been able to witness some outstanding batting.

… DAY 1, SESSION 3 …

Harry Brook and Ollie Pope look to have settled at the wicket and yet another dangerous partnership is brewing for England. Pakistan put on a much better performance in this session. They are finally finding their lengths and troubling the England batters but they need to keep up the intensity in the last session of Day 1. There is still loads of time in the Test match and the game could go either way. Will Pakistan keep their discipline and get more wickets before the end of Day's play? Or will it be England who go into Stumps with their head held high? Join us at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT) to find out.

Despite things looking even in this session, it is England who have the upper hand in the game. Zak Crawley scored the fastest-ever century (86 balls) made by an English opener in Test cricket and his partner Ben Duckett reached his maiden century in a game that he is looking to make a comeback. Pakistan managed to break the 233-run opening partnership and sent both England openers back to the shed in consecutive overs. Joe Root and Ollie Pope put on a 51-run partnership to steady the ship but the dismissal of the former had Pakistan buzzing. Zahid Mahmood bagged two wickets for Pakistan while Haris Rauf chipped in with one.

Session Summary - 27 overs, 158 runs, and 3 wickets. This can be easily considered as a shared session as England have scored runs far too freely and Pakistan have not been able to gain control of the game. It has been an excellent comeback from the Pakistan bowlers in the second session as they have managed to take three wickets on what looks like a difficult pitch for the bowlers. It must be said that the hosts have kept their intensity up and have not lost hope despite the onslaught from the English batters.

Welcome back, ladies and gentlemen! We are all ready for the post-Lunch session as the umpires stride out onto the field. Pakistan will be hoping that the second session will reverse their fortunes and they are able to break this partnership at the earliest. England have a really long batting lineup and they will have to be at the top of their game if they are to get back in this game. England will not want to change their plans as whatever they are doing is working wonders for them. Will they increase this partnership and will more records be broken on the way? Or will the hosts manage to find a breakthrough? Do join us at 1.10 pm IST (7.40 am GMT) to find out.

The openers have put on a massive 174-run partnership in just 164 balls to make this England’s session without any doubt. Zak Crawley thumped 14 runs in the first over, the most runs that have been scored by England in the opening over of a Test match in over a century. He continued his onslaught and got to his half-century in quick time before going into the break with 91 runs in his kitty. Ben Duckett was slightly more watchful but gathered momentum to reach his half-century and ended the session unbeaten on 77. This is the first time two opening batters have got to their half-centuries at a better strike rate than 100 in the same innings of a Test match. The Pakistan bowlers will be disappointed with their effort as they were not able to put the shackles on the scoring with no maidens being bowled in the game so far.

We have had an entertaining first session of Test cricket as England have gotten off to a dream start in this first Test match and are well on course to post a mammoth total. Pakistan have lacked the rhythm and do not look like taking wickets as they have lacked penetration. The pitch has provided no assistance and Ben Stokes will be absolutely thrilled about winning the toss and electing to bat first.

Pakistan would have been waiting for this opportunity to play against a formidable England side in home conditions. They have announced their playing eleven this morning and have given four of their players an opportunity to make their Test debut. Saud Shakeel, Mohammad Ali, Haris Rauf, and Zahid Mahmood will be handed their Test cap before the game and this could be the beginning of a new era for the Asian giants in Test cricket. They have a solid batting lineup that is acquainted with accumulating runs freely and a pace bowling attack that could be considered one of the best in the world. However, if they are to get an upper hand over their opponents, they will need to exploit England's weakness against spinning on subcontinent tracks. They still have an opportunity to make it to the finals of the World Test Championship next year and winning this series will push their chances further.

England had announced their playing eleven 48 hours before the game but will most likely have to go with what players they have fit and available. This is a team that has come under new management this year and there are two things evident in their game with the change of setup. They play an attacking brand of cricket in the longest format of the game with the batters given the license to go after the bowling. They also prefer to chase a target in the fourth innings and have done so successfully on several occasions in recent times. The team has been fairly successful with this new approach and it is to be seen if they can keep up with it in the challenging conditions of the subcontinent. Despite their resurgence, they find themselves out of contention for the finals of the World Test Championship but will be eager to seal a series win away from home.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen to our coverage of the first Test in the historic three-match series as England arrive on Pakistan shores after 17 years. The first encounter will occur at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium and until this morning, there were massive doubts about whether the game would take place as more than half of the visiting team found themselves unwell. However, the good news is that the England Cricket Board has informed their Pakistani counterparts that they will be able to field a playing eleven in this game and the match is set to resume at the scheduled time. This will be great news to the home fans who will be keen to witness some enthralling red-ball cricket and let us not forget the crucial Test Championship points that are up for grabs in this series.
